svg.title: Directional keys enforce blue tile placement at four-cell corners
svg.text: Corner-only seating: directional keys independent of the bit
NEW PROPOSAL: each Life cell has four inward tails; the blue underside expects four outward tails.
One Life cell: its four 0 keys
Blue underside: outward tails
Prototype 0 and 1 profiles, same NW tail
Bit 0
Bit 1
The tail encodes orientation.
A separate tab encodes 0/1.
Equal area, distinct profiles: wrong value or direction causes a collision.
Underside recess = exact matching profile. No wildcard cavity.
Test using ALL-ZERO cells: placement must work without help from the data
CORNER: fits
Solid blue = lower plugs; orange outline = expected recesses.
EDGE: blocked
Solid blue = lower plugs; orange outline = expected recesses.
CELL CENTRE: blocked
Solid blue = lower plugs; orange outline = expected recesses.
WHY THIS PRESERVES THE SIX-TILE REDUCTION
The outward pattern rotates into itself. Rotating the whole tile moves values and key directions together.
Value regions alone cannot enforce the offset: a uniform field would admit the wrong placement.
Verified: 65,536 candidate placements; only (16,16) modulo the 32-unit Life-cell pitch seats correctly.
Includes every 0/1 input combination, all four quarter-turns, and every integer horizontal/vertical offset.
Ideal extrusion proposal, not print-ready CAD. Smooth droplets, tolerances, body alignment and attachment remain to be designed.
Profiles shown here are exact voxel shapes. The TOP 4x4 outputs need the appropriate keys for the next layer, designed separately.
